Carla M: handing off oncall to @Kevin L — I'm off at 4pm PT. Quick FYI: saw a brief spike of 5xx from runtime-west this morning, auto-recovered after a scale-up. No customer-facing errors observed, but p99 jumped. I left a short checklist in the runbook under 'runtime-west/2026-03-17'.

Kevin L: thanks — noted. Two quick clarifications before you go: 1) If we see OOMs inside the model process (OOMKill in container) do we page runtime or SRE? 2) What thresholds should turn a normal investigation into an incident (P1/P2)?

Carla M: good Qs. My read: model-process OOMs -> runtime first (they own model process and model-version rollbacks). Node-level oom/eviction or kube-scheduler failures -> SRE. For incident threshold I'd propose: customer-visible error rate >1% sustained for 5m or any full-region unavailability = P1. Anything noisy but not customer impacting = P2/investigation. Open to tweaks.

Ben S: +1 on the ownership split. Small tweak on threshold: use 2% error rate OR 5xx spikes affecting multiple downstream routes as the P1 trigger. Also, if latency p99 degrades >3x the baseline for >10m AND correlates with increased 5xx, escalate to P1. We should add explicit rules to the playbook.

Ameera R: suggestion — add a short checklist step for cache/warmup problems (KV cache cold starts often look like model OOMs but are separate). If cache warmup fails and you see cold-start tail latency, page runtime first and include the cache-warmup logs (path: /var/log/runtime/cache-warmup.log). I'll paste a quick command to grab logs.

Ameera R: ```
# fetch recent cache/warmup lines
sudo journalctl -u runtime-cache -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 100
# query metrics we want in a page
./ops/query-metrics --range 15m --metrics p50,p95,p99,err_rate --filter region=runtime-west,model_version=latest
```

Kevin L: perfect, thanks @Ameera R. For oncall paging etiquette: page runtime on application-level failures (5xx, model OOMs, misroutes). Page SRE when nodes/instances are unhealthy, kube control-plane errors, or datacenter/network issues. If it's clearly cross-cutting (e.g., node oom causing model failures) page both but annotate which one you think is primary.

Kevin L: also, quick ask for any paged person — collect these before escalating: region, p99, error rate, top 3 models by request volume, model-version, node list, and recent deploys. Example command to get p99 + errors quickly: ```./ops/query-metrics --range 10m --metrics p99,err_rate --filter region=runtime-west```

Carla M: I'll update the runbook now and open a PR to infra/runbooks with the ownership bullets and the P1/P2 thresholds. PR will also add the cache-warmup snippet. Leaving the runbook pointer in the handoff note: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/runbooks/blob/main/runtime-oncall.md#runtime-west

Ben S: small note re: fallback — if runtime can't recover and customer impact is large, follow the 'fallback-to-downgrade' routing policy in routing-configs (not an oncall immediate change, but part of escalation checklist). If you need to trigger it, @Ben S or @Kevin L should be looped in to coordinate.
